source.title: Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models
source.authors: Jie Li; Youming Tao; Bo-Wei He; Meng Ding

page_placements.theme: Robustness defenses and alternatives, and the limits of their robustness

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests recovery after unlearning via targeted and benign fine-tuning, and reports that base methods permit recovery while its UMU defense reduces it. It also argues that low recovery can result from lost plasticity, qualifying the claim.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's reported base-unlearning scores, selected fine-tuning attack scores, and GD new-task scores. Fine-tuning recovery results cited from other papers are not included. The study does not test activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery.
record.test_reason: The study runs relearning attacks (fine-tuning on 10% of the forget set, and benign Alpaca fine-tuning) on GD-, RMU- and KLUE-unlearned Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen3-4B models on TOFU and FaithUn. It reports how far forget-set scores recover, which bears on A and B. It then evaluates its own defense (UMU) against the same attacks, which bears on F. It also argues that low relearning alone can hide a loss of plasticity, which qualifies how robust-unlearning claims (F) should be measured. It does not test C, D or E.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that base unlearning suppresses rather than removes target knowledge, since retraining (and, weakly, benign tuning) restores it. They report that UMU reduces harmful and benign relearning while improving new-task learning. Their ablation, where a pre-update reference gives similarly low relearning with worse plasticity, supports the claim that robust unlearning should block recovery without blocking learning. Note an internal inconsistency: the abstract reports a 30.4-point average harmful reduction, the body 28.8 at p=0.1.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Update-Matched Unlearning on top of GD, RMU, or KLUE; rehearses fine-tuning updates and selects checkpoints using new-task learning trials rather than reproducing a cited unlearning method.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack outcome varies by base method, model, benchmark, and targeted versus benign fine-tuning. UMU's effect is reported across these settings; Table 1 also reports different outcomes at p = 0.1 and p = 0.3, with the p = 0.3 values omitted here.

fits_no_version.finding: Base unlearning lowers AGNews new-task accuracy by 3.9-8.6 points; UMU restores most of it. A pre-update-reference variant (w/o replay) reaches equally low relearning, but its NS falls below even undefended GD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low relearning scores after a robust-unlearning defense can reflect lost plasticity rather than selective resistance.

record.problems: Reported attack scores are averages over three data-order repetitions, but no error bars or significance tests are stated. The paper's own limitations note that rehearsal and evaluated attacks use low-rank adaptation and that full-parameter and adaptive attacks remain future work.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 p = 0.3 harmful-attack scores and non-GD utility/new-task scores; Table 2 ablations; Figure 2 diagnostics; Figure 4 and Table 3 full learning/recovery trajectory; and Table 4 examples are not included to keep the row set focused. Table 1 p = 0.3 results are omitted despite being reported separately.

untested.parts: Prompt-based and internal attacks; no comparison against a never-trained model. General-ability (US) results exist in Table 1 but are not in the rows.
Only 10%/30% forget-subset retraining and Alpaca/AGNews benign tuning were tested, all with LoRA. No loosely related, same-syntax relearning data.
UMU was not tested against full-parameter or adaptive fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization or prompting (the authors' stated limitation).

missing.what: Harmful Attack p=0.3 scores for all base and UMU methods (e.g. RMU TOFU Llama 90.97; GD 51.73)
Benign Attack scores for base RMU/KLUE and RMU+UMU/KLUE+UMU (e.g. TOFU Llama RMU 20.33 vs RMU+UMU 15.35; FaithUn Llama RMU 14.29, KLUE 28.33)
Retention (RS) and Utility (US) scores for base methods, showing general ability is kept at release (e.g. TOFU Llama GD US 92.88 vs Default 91.45)
AGNews fine-tuning slowly restores GD's TOFU FS from 19.32 to 22.18, against UMU's 18.45 to 19.33
Ablation: w/o replay gets attack scores as low as full UMU (e.g. 23.89 vs 24.98) but lower NS (78.91 vs 85.16)
Qualitative examples: GD after a p=0.3 attack returns target answers almost verbatim; GD+UMU does not

record.verdict_notes: All row version codes (V1/V2/V6) were remapped to A/B/F. UMU rows are linked to F only, not B. FaithUn attack scores are computed on questions answered incorrectly at release, and chance level is not stated (stopping threshold 0.33), so low FaithUn recoveries are hard to read. F verdicts come from the method's own authors; only LoRA attacks with a three-rate grid were tested, and no error bars are given. TOFU release FS is set by a chance-like stopping threshold, so near-chance suppression in A holds by construction.

versions.untested_parts: No direct comparison to a model that never learned the target knowledge; general-ability scores are included only for GD below. Other base-method utility results and UMU utility results are not extracted.
Tests targeted fine-tuning on 10% of the forget set and benign Alpaca fine-tuning; does not test loosely related examples, rephrasing, or other recovery mechanisms.
No activation-direction ablation or causal test of access-blocking versus deletion.
No prompt-only, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
UMU is evaluated against targeted and benign fine-tuning attacks, not activation edits, quantization, or prompt-only attacks.

relation.reason: Its relearning attacks on base and UMU models bear on A, B and F.

tranche.reason: Base-method retraining shows suppression rather than removal (against A). The paper argues low relearning alone can mask lost plasticity, backed by the w/o-replay ablation, so F-type robustness claims need restating.

source_check.notes: Attack scores are the max over 5 epochs x 3 LRs, averaged over 3 data orders, which inflates small rises (r37, r39). FaithUn attacks score only questions wrong at release (start 0; threshold 0.33). FaithUn Alpaca results (r41, r43) also support A but sit in no A verdict.

statements.correction: FaithUn Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct GD: release 0.0; p=0.1 48.13; p=0.3 54.76; benign Alpaca 33.33; benchmark threshold accuracy 0.33 (Table 1; Appendix C).
statements.problem: The FaithUn numbers come from Table 1 FaithUn GD cells, but the cited rows r13 and r37 are TOFU rows. The text calls 0.33 the FaithUn benchmark threshold, not chance.

statements.correction: TOFU Forget01 GD Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct: release 19.32 -> 45.41 at p=0.1 (retrained on 4 questions, scored on the other 36). Max over 5 epochs x 3 LRs, averaged over 3 data orders; LoRA.
statements.problem: Minor: 'maximum over steps' in conditions; the score is the maximum over epochs and a learning-rate grid.

statements.correction: 1,000 Alpaca: GD Llama 19.32 -> 20.98; Qwen3 20.03 -> 21.60 (max over epochs/LR grid, 3 data orders averaged).
FaithUn Llama RMU 0.0 -> 52.63 (p=0.1); TOFU Llama RMU 14.04 -> 87.97 vs Default 90.42.
statements.problem: The cited row r27 is FaithUn; the TOFU 'nearly fully restored' rests on r15. The FaithUn attack pool is questions answered wrong at release, so 0 is by construction. 'Maximum over steps' should be over epochs and learning rates.

statements.correction: TOFU Llama GD 19.32 -> 20.98 with 1,000 Alpaca; AGNews tuning lifts the same GD model 19.32 -> 22.18 (Table 3), which the authors call partial restoration.
statements.problem: 'Not restored' is a fair grouping for +1.66. The authors, though, read benign and AGNews rises as partial restoration.

statements.correction: GD TOFU FS 19.32 -> 20.98 under 1,000 Alpaca instructions (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct).
FaithUn Llama p=0.1: GD+UMU 11.11 vs GD 48.13; RMU+UMU 15.79 vs RMU 52.63. The attacks use low-rank adaptation (Limitations).

UMU attacks: LoRA; AdamW for up to 5 epochs; LR grid {1e-5, 5e-6, 1e-6} (benign {1e-5, 1e-6, 1e-7}); max over epochs and LRs; 3 data orders averaged. Full-parameter and adaptive attacks are left to future work.
statements.problem: 'UMU LoRA attacks only' is right. But UMU's attacks do vary data order and sweep a learning-rate grid, so grouping it with 'one recipe' and 'no hyperparameter search' overstates.

statements.correction: UMU, TOFU Forget01, p=0.1: Llama GD+UMU 24.98, KLUE+UMU 24.04, RMU+UMU 52.34; Qwen3-4B GD+UMU 24.64, KLUE+UMU 24.41, RMU+UMU 53.00 (Table 1).
statements.problem: Cites r14 and r16 but gives no UMU content. Those rows do show base-method sensitivity, so a UMU sentence is missing.

statements.correction: Base methods lower NS by 3.91-8.60 points. w/o replay attack scores are similar to UMU (e.g. 23.89 vs 24.98), and its NS falls below GD in all four settings (78.91<82.03, 81.64<83.98, 78.91<80.86, 81.25<83.59).
statements.problem: Minor: the cited rows are GD/GD+UMU NS only. The 8.6 is FaithUn Llama RMU, and the w/o-replay claim comes from Table 2.
